issues.description: Spec requires minimum 1 wei increase when parent gas used exceeds target, but implementation computes feeDelta as parentBaseFee*gasDelta/target/denominator with no lower bound. When the computed delta is 0 (low baseFee or small gasDelta) baseFee stays equal to parentBaseFee instead of parentBaseFee+1.
issues.potential_impact: Consensus failure / chain split versus spec-compliant clients and execution-spec reference (which uses max(..., Uint(1))). Base fee can stall at 0 or very low values, breaking fee-market liveness and allowing zero-fee congestion.
issues.suggestion: Enforce minimum increase: feeDelta = max(target_fee_gas_delta // BASE_FEE_MAX_CHANGE_DENOMINATOR, Wei.ONE) in the parentBlockGasUsed > targetGasUsed branch, matching execution-spec calculate_base_fee_per_gas.

issues.description: Implementation introduces a 7 wei floor (baseFeeFloor, satisfiesFloorTxFee requiring txn gasPrice/maxFee >= 7) that has no counterpart in EIP-1559. Spec allows base fee to decay toward zero via repeated decreases and only requires max_fee_per_gas >= base_fee_per_gas.
issues.potential_impact: Over-strict mempool/block-building filtering: spec-valid transactions with max_fee <7 when baseFee <7 are rejected, causing mempool divergence, UX degradation, and potential validator profit / inclusion differences. If ever enforced in block validation it would cause consensus split.
issues.suggestion: Remove consensus-affecting floor or gate it explicitly as non-consensus spam-protection for txpool only; ensure block validation and computeBaseFee use pure spec formula with no 7-wei clamp.

summary: Base-fee formula ordering and fork-block initial value match spec, but the increase path omits the required max(...,1) minimum, a consensus-critical deviation also present in the execution-spec reference. An additional Besu-specific 7-wei floor has no basis in EIP-1559.
